newsitem.title: USA: First Chicago studies value of bank names.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago studies value of bank names.

text.p: What's in a name? That is the age-old question that First Chicago NBD Corp is trying to answer with a survey to assess the value its three banking brand names.

The holding company, formed by the merger of Chicago-based First Chicago Corp and Detroit-based NBD Bancorp Inc in 1995, operates banks under three names: First National Bank of Chicago, a consumer and small-business bank in Illinois, with large national and international corporate clients; NBD Bank, a consumer and middle-market business bank in Michigan and Indiana; and American National Bank, a middle-market business bank in Illinois.
According to a memo sent to bank employees, First Chicago is trying to determine the value of those names through a survey conducted by Opinion Research of Princeton, New Jersey.
The survey, begun late last month, will include responses from more than 1,000 employees, customers and members of the financial community, the memo said.
First Chicago would not say if the survey would lead to a new name for any of its units.
"This is really a step to say what's the equity in our names," First Chicago spokesman Tom Kelly said. "You have to figure out what you've got and decide if there's anything you need to do about it."
The answers to the survey will help the company determine marketing, public relations, internal and external communications and other corporate identity needs, the memo said.
